findings.text: The 64-bit compressed entry accepts control from the 32-bit stub or straight from a 64-bit loader, starts with interrupts off and direction cleared, establishes flat data segments, keeps the loader boot parameters pointer alive across helper calls, and expects an identity mapping that already covers kernel image plus boot parameters and command line.
Compressed 64-bit entry offset 0x200 is an immutable ABI value.

Decompressed base is chosen as load address rounded up to 2M granularity using loader alignment, clamped to at least the linked physical base, with init size minus compressed end giving relocation target and stack anchored at relocated boot stack end.

Paging mode reconciliation keeps only PAE plus MCE plus LA57 bits from control register, clears flags, funnels level changes through low memory trampoline with relocated top table, reloads global table with 32-bit code entry and refreshes code segment through far return before C helpers.

Early 64-bit flow orders stage1 interrupt setup, then confidential guest enablement, then paging level configuration, then backward copy of compressed image to make in place expansion safe, then table register repoint to relocated copy, then jump to relocated continuation.
Page table work area descriptor holds a byte buffer base plus total capacity plus consumed offset used as bump allocator cursor.
Bump allocator refuses allocation once cursor reaches capacity and reports running low once a warning threshold is hit, advancing cursor by one page on success.
Default kernel PTE mask starts as all bits set and is marked for frequent read access.
Page offset base and setup marker are provided as compile time constants for compressed identity mapping build.
Top level table address is held in a single static, physical address mask starts from physical mask width and later excludes memory encryption mask.
Identity range helper aligns start down and end up to large page size, does nothing when range is empty or inverted, otherwise extends current top table and reports failure through error helper.

Identity table initialization resets allocator cursor, reuses existing boot tables when entered from 32-bit path and otherwise allocates fresh top table, maps kernel image plus boot parameters plus command line plus chained setup data, prepares confidential guest tables, loads new table and checks SNP feature compatibility.
Mapping descriptor is populated with bump allocator callback plus context plus large executable page flags combined with encryption mask plus table entry flags.
Debug address helper has two builds, one emitting label plus hex value and newline and one compiling to nothing, so diagnostic coverage depends on build selection.
Decrypted page helper clears encryption attribute on one address through generic flag update path.

Flag update ensures a mapping exists by touching the address, descends to PMD level, splits large entries when present, flushes caches on encryption changes, orders shared transition before table update and private transition after, then flushes translation cache by reloading top table.

Large to small split assumes sole ownership of tables and absence of concurrent users, so skipping separate purge between PMD clear and rewrite is claimed safe from multihit even though target range may hold running code or stack.

Large split allocates one fresh page for small entries, derives small flags by dropping large page bit, populates full fanout with ascending page addresses, installs new PMD and flushes translation cache before returning entry for requested address.
Cache line purge uses fixed 64 byte stride over one page with memory fence first, avoiding processor feature queries that could fault before guest communication is ready.
Compressed stage address translation is identity, returning input value unchanged.
Unsupported SNP feature query returns zero when SNP is off, otherwise reports requested features that lack guest implementation.

SNP compatibility check aborts boot when unsupported features exist, passing offending mask through guest hypervisor channel when available and falling back to direct termination when channel version or setup is insufficient.
Early guest communication setup decrypts and clears dedicated page, publishes it as active channel, initializes instruction decoding tables and registers channel address when SNP is active.
SNP enabled predicate tests SNP enabled bit inside cached status word.
Page privacy helpers do nothing unless SNP is active, otherwise request private or shared state for one page using boot secure service context.
Default builds provide empty SNP page state, identity preparation and feature check helpers that perform no action.

Page state change preserves guest channel register, validates ordering with invalidate before shared request and validate after private request, issues hypervisor exit for table update, terminates boot on unexpected reply, then restores saved register.
Guest channel register access goes through raw model specific register reads and writes on SEV ES channel register.
Direct termination path reports set plus reason through channel register, exits to hypervisor and then halts forever.
GHCB based termination invalidates channel structure, records termination exit code plus two info words, publishes channel address and exits to hypervisor before halting forever.

Four K validation branches on privilege level, using secure service call when virtualized privilege is present and native validation otherwise, terminating on failure and applying cache eviction mitigation when making pages private on affected hardware.

Secure service validation builds single entry request with 4K size plus validate flag plus frame number in shared buffer, saves interrupt state with native primitives, issues core validation call by MSR protocol and terminates on protocol failure before restoring interrupts.
Secure service validation runs with native interrupt save around MSR protocol and restores prior flag state afterwards, avoiding paravirtualized helpers during very early boot.
MSR protocol wrapper repeats call while result indicates busy or incomplete.

MSR protocol saves channel register, requests privilege level zero service, issues call, captures response, restores saved value, rejects pending calls plus wrong response codes plus nonzero status, otherwise maps service result codes.
Service result mapping treats success as done, busy plus incomplete as retryable, and all other codes as invalid.
Service issue passes five registers into virtual machine call, marks call pending with atomic exchange and captures five output registers plus prior pending flag.
Flag update returns out of memory when large split cannot allocate a fresh page, leaving mapping unchanged.
Termination paths never return, spinning in halt after hypervisor exit, so callers must not expect recovery.
